url: /kanvas/guides/snapshots/helm-kanvas-snapshot/index.md
description: Generate a rendered image of a Helm chart from the command line with the Kanvas Snapshot Helm plugin, and receive it by URL or email.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Kanvas Snapshot Helm plugin renders a Helm chart as a Kanvas design image from your terminal. Use it to see what a chart deploys before you install it, or to put a picture of a chart in a review, a ticket, or a README. It needs no repository, no cluster, and no Layer5 Cloud account.

You give the plugin the URL of a packaged chart. The plugin imports the chart as a design, starts a render, and then prints the image URL or emails you when the image is ready.

## Before you start

- Helm installed on your machine.
- A packaged chart (`.tgz`) at a URL that the snapshot service can download without credentials. The plugin submits the value of `-f` as a URL, so a local file path is not a supported input.
- For email delivery, an address in lowercase.

## Install the plugin

```bash
helm plugin install https://github.com/meshery/helm-kanvas-snapshot
```

The install downloads a prebuilt binary for your platform. Confirm the install and update it later with:

```bash
helm plugin list
helm plugin update helm-kanvas-snapshot
```

The list shows the plugin as `helm-kanvas-snapshot`. Helm runs a plugin by its name, so the command is `helm helm-kanvas-snapshot`.

## Generate a snapshot

```bash
helm helm-kanvas-snapshot -f <chart-url> [--name <name>] [-e <email>]
```

For example:

```bash
helm helm-kanvas-snapshot -f https://meshery.github.io/meshery.io/charts/meshery-v1.0.20.tgz --name meshery-chart
```

| Flag | Required | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `-f`, `--file` | Yes | URL of the packaged chart. |
| `--name` | No | Name of the design that the plugin creates. Without it, the plugin uses the file name without its extension and prints a warning that it did. |
| `-e`, `--email` | No | Email address to notify when the snapshot is ready. The plugin rejects any address that contains uppercase letters or does not look like an address, and exits with an error. |

## What happens

1. The plugin imports the chart as a saved design and prints `Successfully created Meshery design. ID: <id>`.
2. The plugin starts the rendering workflow.
3. The plugin prints the result and exits.

Without `--email`, the plugin prints the snapshot URL. The image takes three to five minutes to appear at that URL, so an immediate request can return nothing. With `--email`, the plugin prints a confirmation and the service emails you when the snapshot is ready.

## Privacy and ownership

The plugin ships with Layer5's service credentials, so it works without signing in. That has three consequences:

- The service downloads your chart from the URL you give. Use only a chart that you are willing to expose to that service.
- The image sits at a public URL named after the design id. Anyone who has the URL can open it.
- The plugin saves the design with the service's credentials, not under a Layer5 Cloud account of yours. To work on a chart as your own design, import it into Kanvas instead. See [Import and Merge Designs]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designs/import-designs/index.md" >}}).

## Errors

The plugin exits with status 1 and prints an error code.

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `kanvas-snapshot-900` | The chart URI is invalid. |
| `kanvas-snapshot-901` | The plugin could not create the design. |
| `kanvas-snapshot-902` | The plugin could not start the render. |
| `kanvas-snapshot-903` | An HTTP request failed. |
| `kanvas-snapshot-905` | A response could not be decoded. |
| `kanvas-snapshot-906` | A request returned an unexpected status. The message carries the status and the response body. |
| `kanvas-snapshot-907` | A required field is missing. |
| `kanvas-snapshot-908` | The email address is not valid. |
| `kanvas-snapshot-909` | GitHub rejected the request to start the render with a 401 or 403 status. |

If the image never appears, check that the chart URL opens in a browser without signing in, then run the command again. For pull request snapshots, see [Visualize Pull Requests with Kanvas Snapshot]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/snapshots/kanvas-snapshot/index.md" >}}).


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Stream Container Logs"
url: /kanvas/guides/operating/log-streaming/index.md
description: Live-tail the logs of a pod or container from the Operator canvas, search the stream, and know its limits.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Log streaming live-tails the output of a pod's containers inside the Operator canvas. Each stream starts with the most recent lines and then follows new output as it is written, so you can watch a rollout, a crash loop, or a request path next to the topology that produced it.

## Before you start

- **Operator mode on a Meshery you run.** The hosted kanvas.new site does not offer Operator mode.
- **A connected cluster with Meshery Operator deployed.** MeshSync reads the logs and Meshery Server relays them through the broker, the same path the terminal uses. See [Operator]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/operator/index.md" >}}).
- **Containers that exist.** Logs come from the Kubernetes log API, so a container that has not started has nothing to stream.

## Start a stream

The action is named **Initiate Log Session** and is offered on **Pod** and **Container** resources only. Right-click the resource, or select it and use the action in the header of the Details panel. The stream opens in the same bottom-left panel as [terminal sessions]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/operating/interactive-terminal/index.md" >}}), as a tab.

| You select | Tabs opened |
|---|---|
| A pod | One tab for the pod that combines every container in its `containers` list. Each line is prefixed with `[<pod>:<container>]` in a per-container color. |
| A container | One tab for that container. |
| Several pods, one after another | One tab per pod. Kanvas does not merge different pods into one tab. |

Starting a stream for a pod that already has a tab does nothing. To stream only some of a pod's containers, use the container selector in the panel header. Choosing different containers restarts that tab's stream.

## Read and control the stream

- **Backlog.** Each container starts with its last 1,000 lines. Kanvas requests timestamps, so every line begins with an RFC 3339 time. Standard output and standard error arrive combined.
- **Scrollback.** The browser keeps the last 10,000 lines per tab.
- **Search.** The search icon in the panel header opens a search field with next and previous controls. It highlights and jumps between matches. It does not hide non-matching lines.
- **Copy.** Select text in the stream to copy it. There is no Clear, Copy-all, or Download control.
- **Stop.** The trash icon on a tab stops the stream and removes the tab. Closing the panel with its close button only hides it; streams keep running.

Empty lines are dropped. Very long lines can be split across messages and display broken.

## Limits and scope

| Item | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Initial backlog | 1,000 lines per container, fixed. |
| Previous container logs | Not available. Streams read the current container only. |
| Follow | Always on. |
| Reconnect | None. If the connection drops, the tab stops updating with no message. Close it and start a new stream. |
| Container exits or pod is deleted | The stream ends with no message. |
| Resource names | Pod, namespace, and container names must be valid Kubernetes DNS labels. Other names are rejected by the server. |
| Changing the container selection | Requests the 1,000-line backlog again, so lines can repeat in the tab. |

## Who can use it

Kanvas does not hide or disable the action by role or plan. The permission model lists **Stream container logs** as an Operator capability for the Team Operator plan and above, granted to workspace administrators, organization administrators, and provider administrators. See [Permissions by Role]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/permissions.md" >}}) and [Feature Availability]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/feature-availability.md" >}}).

## Failure modes

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| Panel shows `Failed to create terminal session` with a reason | The Kanvas extension could not be loaded by Meshery, for example because it was built for a different Meshery version. Install matching versions. |
| Toast `No container found to create log session` | The selected component lists no containers. |
| Empty tab, no lines | The pod has produced no output, or Meshery Server cannot reach MeshSync. Confirm the cluster shows as connected and that the broker is connected. Kanvas does not display the server's error text for log streams. |

For cluster connection problems, see [Troubleshoot Kanvas]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/troubleshooting.md" >}}).

## Related

- [Run a Performance Test]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/operating/performance-testing/index.md" >}}) to see how a service holds up under load while the stream is open.
- [Operator]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/operator/index.md" >}}) explains the data path from the cluster to the canvas.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Canvas Objects"
url: /kanvas/reference/canvas-objects/index.md
description: Reference for every object on the Designer canvas - components, shapes, sections, textboxes, images and edges - covering how each is added, what you can do to it, its style options, defaults and limits.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Everything on a Designer canvas is an object, and every object answers to the same small set of actions: add, select, copy, duplicate, lock, restyle, resize and delete. This page lists each object kind, each action, every style option and the limits that apply. Edges - the lines that connect objects - have their own section at the end.

Designer mode only. In Operator mode you cannot add, edit, duplicate, delete or rename objects, and live nodes discovered from a cluster are read-only in every mode. See [Designer]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/designer/index.md" >}}) for how the two modes differ.

## Object kinds {#canvas-objects}

| Object | What it is | Configurable | Added from |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Component** | A piece of infrastructure under management, such as a Deployment, an S3 bucket or a Lambda function. | Yes. It carries configuration and is part of what gets deployed. | The Components and Kubernetes pickers in the dock, a file import, or a drop |
| **Shape** | A visual primitive: a circle, an arrow, a flowchart symbol or a cloud-provider glyph. | No | The Shapes picker in the dock |
| **Section** | A labeled frame that fences off a region. Objects dropped inside it become its children and move with it. | No | The Section tool in the dock, or <kbd>S</kbd> |
| **Textbox** | A resizable box whose content is text. | No | The Textbox tool in the dock, or <kbd>T</kbd> |
| **Image** | A picture embedded in the design. | No | <kbd>I</kbd>, the Image tool in the dock, or a file drop |
| **Comment** | A threaded note pinned to the canvas. See [Reviewing Designs]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/collaborating/reviewing-designs/index.md" >}}). | No | <kbd>M</kbd> or the Comment tool in the dock |
| **Pencil stroke** and **pen point** | Freehand drawings and the joints of drawn lines. See [Tool Modes]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/tool-modes/index.md" >}}). | No | The Pencil and Pen tools |

Every object except a component is an **annotation**. Kanvas stores annotations in the design alongside components, but treats them differently:

| Behavior | Annotation | Configurable component |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Layers panel toggle | **Annotations** | **Configurable Components** |
| Kind name appended to the on-canvas label | No | Yes |
| Has configuration to edit | No | Yes |
| Counts toward the components-per-design limit of your plan when the design is saved | Yes | Yes |

The plan limit counts every entry in a design, drawn objects included, so a heavily annotated design can reach the limit sooner than its infrastructure alone suggests. See [Feature Availability by Plan]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/feature-availability.md" >}}).

## Adding objects {#adding-objects}

| Method | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Drag from a dock picker onto the canvas | The object lands where you release it. |
| Click an icon in a picker | The object lands at a random position near the center of the canvas. |
| <kbd>M</kbd>, <kbd>T</kbd>, <kbd>S</kbd> | Adds a comment, textbox or section near the center of the canvas. A textbox opens ready for typing. |
| <kbd>I</kbd> | Opens a file picker for an image. |
| Drop or paste a file | See the file rules below. |
| Paste a copied selection | Adds the copied objects and the relationships between them at the pointer. |

A newly added component opens its configurator beside the node. A textbox starts inline text editing on double-click. Shapes accept body text too, so double-click a shape to type in it.

### Shapes {#adding-shapes}

The Shapes picker lists the shape libraries registered in Meshery, with search across all of them. A default installation includes libraries for cloud providers (Amazon Web Services, Azure, Google Cloud Platform), developer icons, arrows, flowchart symbols, general-purpose shapes and line icons. The libraries come from the registry, so the list can differ between installations. Pin a library to the dock to keep it one action away - see [Pinning a Model to the Dock]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designing/pin-model-to-dock/index.md" >}}).

<figure>
  <img src="images/shape-libraries.png" alt="The Shapes picker open in Kanvas Designer, listing the available shape libraries" />
  <figcaption>The Shapes picker lists every shape library available to your design</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure>
  <img src="images/shapes-library-expanded.png" alt="The built-in Shapes library expanded, showing its shape primitives" />
  <figcaption>A shape library expanded</figcaption>
</figure>

### Sections {#adding-sections}

A section draws its label along its top edge instead of through its middle, so the region it encloses stays readable. Drop other objects inside it and they move with the section. Deleting the section does not delete them.

### Textboxes {#adding-textboxes}

<figure>
  <img src="images/textbox-on-canvas.png" alt="A textbox on the Kanvas Designer canvas with a dashed border, a transparent fill and the caption 'Ingress tier - north/south traffic'" />
  <figcaption>A textbox carrying a caption</figcaption>
</figure>

### Files dropped or pasted on the canvas {#files}

| File | Result | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Any image type the browser recognizes | An image object. The picture is embedded in the design as data, not linked. | 512,000 bytes (about 500 KB) |
| Plain text (`.txt`) | A textbox holding the file text. | 512,000 bytes (about 500 KB) |
| YAML, JSON, TAR, GZ, TGZ, ZIP, RAR, 7Z | An infrastructure-as-code import at the drop position. See [Importing Designs]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designs/import-designs/index.md" >}}). | Import rules apply |
| Any other type | Ignored with no message | - |

Files over the size limit are rejected with an error message. The limit is fixed and is the same on every plan. A file with no browser-reported type is classified by its extension.

## Selecting objects {#selecting}

| Gesture | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Click | Selects one object and shows its style toolbar. |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + click | Adds or removes one object from the selection. |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + drag on empty canvas | Draws a selection box. Box selection is off in Pan, Pen and Pencil modes. |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> | Selects every component on the canvas. |

Dragging selected objects moves them together. Locked objects do not move.

## Actions on objects {#object-menu}

Right-click an object, or press and hold on it, to open its menu. Each entry appears only when its condition holds.

| Action | Shortcut | Appears when | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Copy | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> | Designer mode, object is not a group | Menu: copies that one object. Keyboard: copies the whole selection and every relationship whose two ends are both selected. |
| Duplicate | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>D</kbd> | Designer mode, not a group | Adds a copy to the same design. |
| Lock | - | Designer mode, not a group, not locked | Fixes the object's position. |
| Unlock | - | The object is locked | Releases the position. |
| Delete | <kbd>Delete</kbd> or <kbd>Backspace</kbd> | Designer mode, not a group | Removes the object. The keys delete the whole selection. |
| Reset styles | - | The object supports style changes | Restores the object's default styling. |
| Group | - | A multi-selection | Turns the temporary selection group into a permanent group. |
| Ungroup | - | A permanent group | Dissolves the group. |
| Move Out of Parent | - | Designer mode, the object sits inside a parent | Takes the object out of its parent. |

<figure>
  <img src="images/object-context-menu.png" alt="The circular context menu open on a selected object in Kanvas Designer, with Lock, Reset styles, Copy, Duplicate and Delete around the object" />
  <figcaption>The context menu open on a selected object</figcaption>
</figure>

Every change an action makes, restyling included, is a change to the shared design, so <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Z</kbd> reverses it. See [Canvas Actions]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/canvas-actions/index.md" >}}).

### Copy and paste {#copying}

Copy writes the object data to your system clipboard. Paste with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> into the same design, a different design or another browser tab running Kanvas.

- Pasted objects land at the pointer when it is over the canvas, otherwise at the canvas center, and keep their relative layout.
- Every pasted object receives a new identifier. Styling travels with the copy.
- The browser must allow clipboard access. If it refuses, nothing happens and no message appears.

### Duplicate {#cloning}

Duplicate skips the clipboard. It places the copy 50 pixels right and 50 pixels down from the original, gives it a new identifier and copies the relationships between members of the duplicated set. Duplicating a section together with its children reproduces the whole arrangement. Names are unchanged.

### Lock {#locking}

A lock fixes position only. A locked object can still be selected, restyled, configured and deleted, but it cannot be dragged, directly or inside a selection. The lock is stored with the object, so it survives a reload and applies to collaborators. Locking a section does not lock the objects inside it.

### Delete {#deleting}

Deleting an object also removes the relationships that touch it. Kanvas marks those relationships as deleted rather than discarding them, so the next [policy evaluation]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/relationship-evaluation/index.md" >}}) can undo any configuration they had applied. Deleting a section leaves its children on the canvas. Deletion is immediate and has no confirmation, but it can be undone.

## Style options {#configuring-styles}

Selecting one object shows a style toolbar above it. The toolbar edits the selected object; it does not apply a change to a multi-selection. Each control appears only when the object's definition declares that capability, so the controls you see vary by object. The toolbar appears only when the canvas is zoomed in past a detail threshold; zoomed out, the canvas shows a hint to zoom in.

| Property | Options |
| --- | --- |
| Shape | 24 outlines: ellipse, triangle, round-triangle, rectangle, round-rectangle, bottom-round-rectangle, cut-rectangle, barrel, rhomboid, diamond, round-diamond, pentagon, round-pentagon, hexagon, round-hexagon, concave-hexagon, heptagon, round-heptagon, octagon, round-octagon, star, tag, round-tag, vee. Changing the outline keeps the content. |
| Fill | 13 swatches including transparent, and an opacity slider from 0 to 1 in steps of 0.1. |
| Border | Color from the same swatches, style (solid, dotted, dashed, double) and thickness from 0 to 25. |
| Layer order | Move To Front, Move Forward, Move Backward, Move To Back. |
| Label | The name drawn with the object. |
| Link | An external URL. A link adds an External Link badge, which opens the URL in a new tab. See [Component Badges]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/component-badges/index.md" >}}). |
| Image | A background image, set by URL or by upload, with a reset to the default. |
| Animation | None, blink, ripple, bounce or pulse. |
| Text | Color, weight (Regular, Medium, Semi Bold, Bold, Black), decoration (none, underline, line-through), horizontal alignment (left, center, right), vertical alignment (top, center, bottom) and size. |
| Configure | Opens the configurator. Components only. See [Configuring Components]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designing/configuring-components/index.md" >}}). |

The default text style is gray, 12 pixels, regular weight and centered. Sections carry their label on the top edge rather than body text.

Restyling changes only how an object is drawn. It never changes a component's configuration or what gets deployed.

### Reset styles {#resetting-styles}

Reset styles re-applies the styling recorded in the object's definition and discards every change made in the style toolbar. It restores the definition, not an earlier state, so it is not an undo. Position, lock state, configuration and relationships are untouched.

## Resizing {#resizing}

Select a single object and Kanvas draws eight handles around it, one at each corner and one at the midpoint of each side.

- Drag a corner or side handle to resize.
- Hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> while dragging to keep the aspect ratio.
- Objects that contain other objects, such as a parent component or a section with children, show no handles.

Resizing needs the object's definition to declare the resize capability. The new size is saved with the design.

## Edges {#edges}

An edge is a line between two objects. Each edge is a relationship in the design, and relationships come in two kinds.

| Edge kind | What it represents | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Semantic | A relationship defined in the registry, such as a network connection or a volume mount. | Kanvas updates the configuration of the components it joins as you draw it, and re-evaluates it as the design changes. See [Relationships]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/relationships/index.md" >}}). |
| Annotation | A line you draw with the Pen tool to explain a flow or a dependency. | Visual only. It is non-binding and configures nothing. |

Select an edge to open the edge toolbar.

![Examples of changing edge styles in Kanvas](images/style-edge.gif)

| Control | Options |
| --- | --- |
| Line Color | The same 13 swatches as fills. The arrowhead takes the same color. |
| Line Style | Dotted, Solid, Dashed. |
| Arrow/Curve Style | A curve style and an arrowhead, listed below. |
| Name | A text label drawn on the edge. |
| Edge Animation | None, or marching ants: a dashed line that travels along the edge. |
| Delete | Removes the edge. Works on any edge. |

### Curve styles

| Curve style | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| Bezier | A smooth curve. The default. |
| Straight | A direct line. |
| Segments | A line with two bends. |
| Round segments | Segments with rounded corners. |
| Taxi | Right-angle routing. |
| Round taxi | Right-angle routing with rounded corners. |
| Haystack | A short line that starts and ends inside the nodes. |
| Unbundled bezier | A curve with one adjustable control point. |
| Multi unbundled bezier | A curve with two control points. |
| Straight triangle | A straight line drawn with a triangular profile. |

Choosing a curve style applies its default geometry. Choosing Round taxi does not apply its default corner radius.

### Arrowheads

Vee (the default), triangle, circle, square, diamond, triangle-cross, tee, triangle-tee, circle-triangle, triangle-backcurve and chevron. An arrowhead is drawn at the target end only.

### Edge defaults

A new edge uses a dotted line, a vee arrowhead, a bezier curve, a width of 1.5 pixels and a light gray color. A selected edge draws at 4 pixels. Edges that carry TCP traffic draw as a solid gold line with a triangle-cross arrowhead.

## Permissions {#permission-reference}

Kanvas gates canvas actions by mode and by object capability, not by role. The permission catalog in Layer5 Cloud lists a key for each shape, section, textbox and component-styling action (add, copy, clone, lock, delete, configure styles, reset styles and resize), and organization administrators can include them in roles and keychains. Kanvas does not check those keys on the canvas today, so withholding one does not hide a control.

The permissions Kanvas does enforce on the toolbar are Validate Design, Deploy Design, Undeploy Design and Share Design. See [Permissions by Role]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/permissions.md" >}}).

| Action | Gate | When the gate fails |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Add, duplicate, copy, paste, delete, lock | Designer mode | The control is not offered in Operator mode. |
| Edit a live cluster node | Never allowed | Live nodes are read-only in every mode. |
| Style, reset styles, resize | The object's definition declares the capability | The control is hidden. |
| Pen and Pencil | The Enable Pen and Enable Pencil options | The dock icons are hidden. |

## Limits {#limits}

| Item | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Image file | 512,000 bytes (about 500 KB), same on every plan |
| Text file | 512,000 bytes (about 500 KB), same on every plan |
| Border thickness | 0 to 25 |
| Fill opacity | 0 to 1 |
| Components per design | Set by your plan and enforced when the design is saved. Annotations count. |
| Image count per design | No limit |

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Clone a Design"
url: /kanvas/guides/designs/cloning-a-design/index.md
description: Copy a public or published design into your own workspace to use as a template, and learn what carries over.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Cloning copies a design into your own workspace so you can change it freely. The clone is an independent record: later changes to the source never reach it, and edits to the clone never reach the source.

## What you can clone

The server clones only designs whose visibility is public or published. A request for any other design fails with 403 "unauthorized to clone design". That includes your own private designs. To copy one of those, open it and use Save as. See [Save Designs]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designs/saving-designs/index.md" >}}). A missing source design returns 500 "could not find design".

## Where to start a clone

Kanvas has no Clone item for the design that is open. You clone from these places:

- **The catalog.** The catalog modal's Clone action, and catalog design cards in Layer5 Cloud.
- **A catalog link.** Opening a link with `mode=design&type=catalog&id=<id>` clones that design and opens your copy.
- **Tutorials.** Opening a tutorial's design clones it.

The client names a catalog clone `<design name> (Copy)`, and a tutorial clone `<tutorial title> (Copy)`. The server stores whatever name it receives and rejects an empty request body with 400. When the clone completes, Kanvas loads it. If the open design has unsaved changes, you confirm first.

Layer5 Cloud shows the Clone action only to roles with the Clone Design permission. The server checks visibility, not the key. See [Permissions]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/permissions.md" >}}).

## What carries over

| Carried over | Reset or changed |
|---|---|
| Components, relationships, styles, configuration, annotations, and preferences, converted to the current design format | New id |
| The origin of the source design | Version 0.0.1 |
| Catalog data (compatibility, type, info, caveats, content class, published version, snapshot URLs) | Owner is you |
| | Visibility private |
| | Workspace is your selected workspace |
| | Source file and usage counters are not copied |

Cloning is the only path that creates a private design. Every other new design is public.

## Limits and failure behavior

Cloning does not check your plan's components-per-design limit. A clone from a larger plan can exceed yours and then fail its first autosave with a plan-limit error. See [Save Designs]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designs/saving-designs/index.md" >}}).

Kanvas shows `Cloning design "<name>"` while the clone runs. It shows no failure message. Because the clone copies the catalog data block, a private clone can display catalog metadata even though it is not published.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Deploy a Design"
url: /kanvas/guides/deploying/deploying-designs/index.md
description: Apply a design to one or more Kubernetes clusters, and understand targets, ordering, dependencies, results, and failure behavior.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Deploying applies the components in a design to the Kubernetes clusters in the environments you choose. Meshery Server does the work with the kubeconfig it holds: it creates each object, or updates it in place when it already exists. Deploying the same design again is safe and idempotent.

## Before you start

- **A Meshery you run, with a connected cluster.** The hosted kanvas.new site does not deploy; it shows a self-hosted-feature prompt. Meshery needs at least one connected Kubernetes context that belongs to an environment in your organization.
- **A non-empty design.** The Actions menu is disabled for an empty design. An unsaved design deploys as it stands on the canvas.
- **Permission.** The Deploy Design permission gates the action. See [Permissions by Role]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/permissions.md" >}}). Selecting environments from the empty state also needs the Create Environment and Edit Environment permissions.
- **A provider session.** Without a signed-in session the request fails before any event is raised.

Deploying does not need Meshery Operator, MeshSync, or the broker. Those make the result visible in Operator mode.

Validate and dry-run the design first. See [Validate a Design]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/deploying/validating-designs/index.md" >}}) and [Dry-run a Design]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/deploying/dry-running-a-design/index.md" >}}). The deploy flow runs both for you.

## The deploy flow

Choose Deploy from the design's Actions menu. The `Deploy design "<name>"` stepper has five steps, with Back and Next throughout.

| Step | What it does |
|---|---|
| 1. Validate Design | Runs [validation]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/deploying/validating-designs/index.md" >}}) inline. Next is always enabled, because validation errors are warnings. |
| 2. Identify Environments | Lists your organization's environments as cards. Ticking an environment selects all of its Kubernetes connections. You need at least one. |
| 3. Dry Run | Runs a deploy-type [dry run]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/deploying/dry-running-a-design/index.md" >}}) against the selected clusters. Next stays disabled while it runs, or when errors exist and the bypass checkbox is off. |
| 4. Finalize Deployment | Shows the environments you chose and the component count, excluding annotations. The button reads Deploy. A Schedule Deployment checkbox is shown disabled. |
| 5. Finish | Starts the deployment and shows the results. |

Step 2 shows only Kubernetes connections. When your organization has no environments, it shows `No environments found. Add a new environment.` When an environment has no connections, it shows `No connections configured. Add a connection to get started.` Your selection persists for the session. A cluster that belongs to two selected environments is listed twice and targeted twice.

## Targets

The stepper always sends the explicit clusters you selected. Where no selection exists, such as a one-click action or the mobile sheet, the target is `all`. The server expands a lone `all` to every connected Kubernetes context. Otherwise it keeps only the ids that match a connected context and silently drops unknown ones. If none remain, the request fails with `meshery-server-1096`.

Clusters are deployed in parallel.

## How components are applied

| Aspect | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Ordering | Components form a dependency graph. A component starts when every component it depends on has succeeded. Independent components run in parallel. Kanvas applies no other ordering, so deploy custom resource definitions before the resources that use them. |
| Failed dependency | A component whose dependency failed is withheld: `Withheld <component>: <dependency> did not deploy successfully` (`meshery-server-1480`). |
| Invalid dependencies | A malformed, unknown, ambiguous, or circular dependency fails the whole request before anything is applied (`meshery-server-1475` through `1479`). |
| Existing objects | The object is replaced in place. An update to an immutable field, or an attempt to unset a Service's cluster IP, is reported as success but does not take effect. |
| Namespaces | A missing target namespace is created before the object is applied. A namespaced component with no namespace goes to `default`. |
| Annotation components | Never applied. |

### Dependencies of non-Kubernetes models

For a component whose model is not the built-in Kubernetes model and whose registrant is an Artifact Hub source, Meshery installs the model's source Helm chart into the component's namespace, creating the namespace if needed. This brings in the custom resource definitions and operators the component needs. The step is fail-forward: if the chart fails, Meshery still applies the component and adds a row to the results, `error deploying dependent helm chart for <component>`.

Meshery always processes these dependencies. The Include Dependencies checkbox in the dry-run step does not change this.

### What Meshery marks on applied objects

| Mark | Value |
|---|---|
| Label `design.meshery.io/id` | The design's id |
| Annotation `design.meshery.io/version` | The design's version |
| Annotation `component.meshery.io/id` | The component's id |

Operator's per-design view filters on the design-id label. A component carrying it is shown as managed by Meshery.

## Read the results

Every deployment raises an event from Meshery Server. It appears as a toast and as an entry in the notification center. In the Finish step, a summary lists one row per component and cluster: `Deployed <Kind> "<name>"`, or `Failed to deploy <Kind> "<name>"` with an error card. When Operator is enabled, the step offers Open In Operator.

| Outcome | Event |
|---|---|
| The request completed | `Deployment completed for design '<name>'.` at informational severity |
| The request failed before applying (cluster client, dependency graph, malformed design) | `Failed to deploy design '<name>'.` at error severity, with an error card |

A deployment in which some components failed in Kubernetes still raises the completed event. Read the per-component rows in the Finish step to see which ones failed.

Each persisted deploy event, including an error event, adds 1 to the design's deployment count in Layer5 Cloud. Dry runs and undeploys do not change it. The count drives the catalog sort Most Deployed.

### Error cards

An error card shows the event description, then Details, then Probable Cause and Suggested Remediation side by side. In the notification center, the Error Docs menu item opens the matching entry in the [Meshery error code reference](https://docs.meshery.io/reference/error-codes).

| Code | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `meshery-server-1073` | Unable to deploy the design. Wraps most hard failures; Details holds the inner error. | Confirm the connection's status is Connected or upload a new kubeconfig, and assign the connection to the selected environment. |
| `meshery-server-1096` | Kubernetes cluster is unavailable: no selected context resolved. | Upload a new kubeconfig, check the network and the cluster, and verify the server's credentials. |
| `meshery-server-1095` | Invalid kubeconfig. | Upload a new kubeconfig and make sure the server can reach the API server. |
| `meshery-server-1070` | Failed to parse the design file. | Check the design definition. |
| `meshkit-11190` | Error applying a manifest. The Kubernetes API's own reason and remediation replace the generic text. | Make sure the manifest is valid. |
| `meshery-server-1475` to `1480` | A dependency problem in the design. | Open the design, fix, rename, or remove the dependency, and retry. For 1480, resolve the dependency's failure first. |

## When nothing happens

The Finish step waits for the next deploy event from the server. If the request fails before the server raises an event, such as an expired session, a proxy error, or no provider, Kanvas shows no error and the Finish step keeps spinning. The step has no timeout. Close it, sign in again if your session expired, and check the notification center and the Meshery Server logs.

## Related

- [Undeploy a Design]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/deploying/undeploying-designs/index.md" >}}) removes what a deployment created.
- [Troubleshoot Kanvas]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/troubleshooting.md" >}}) covers connection and loading problems.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Policy Evaluation"
url: /kanvas/concepts/relationship-evaluation/index.md
description: How Kanvas evaluates the relationships in a design continuously, which engine runs the evaluation, what triggers it, and why results can change after you stop editing.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Evaluation is how a design stays consistent. After you change a design, Kanvas runs it through the policy engine, which applies the registry's [relationship]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/relationships/index.md" >}}) definitions: it identifies relationships, writes configuration across related components, and drops relationships that no longer hold. The engine returns the whole evaluated design, and Kanvas applies it back to the canvas. This is why a value you did not touch can change a moment after you edit a related component.

Evaluation never blocks editing. You can keep designing while it runs, and a new edit supersedes the evaluation in progress.

## What triggers evaluation

Evaluation runs after any of these changes:

- A configuration value or a display name changes.
- A relationship is added or removed.
- A component is added, removed, duplicated, or merged.
- A design loads, or an import or merge completes.

Kanvas waits until changes stop for about one second, then evaluates. Another change during evaluation restarts the cycle. Selecting the indicator icon forces an evaluation, and a new design resets evaluation state.

## Two interchangeable engines

| Engine | Where it runs | Properties |
|---|---|---|
| Meshery server | In your Meshery server | Always available. |
| Client-side (WASM) | In a background worker in your browser | No round trips to the server, so it is typically faster. A WASM evaluation times out after 10 seconds. |

Both engines apply the same policy engine and the same definitions. The choice changes where the work happens.

### Choosing the engine

The Relationship Evaluation Engine preference lives in the Options dialog, which you open from the canvas right-click menu.

| Value | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Automatic (recommended) | The default. At load, Kanvas tries to start the WASM engine and waits up to 30 seconds for it to report ready. If it starts, WASM is used. If not, the Meshery server is used. |
| Meshery server | Always uses the server. |
| Client-side (WASM) | Always uses WASM. |

The preference is saved to your user preferences, so it applies on all your devices and designs. Kanvas chooses the engine once, when Designer loads, so reload Kanvas for a change to take effect.

Two behaviors to know:

- Forcing Client-side (WASM) gives no fallback. If the engine fails to start, evaluations fail silently and relationships stop updating. Switch to Automatic or Meshery server and reload.
- Automatic checks only that the engine initializes. It does not fall back to the server later if the WASM engine fails after a successful start.

## Reading the indicator

The top toolbar shows an icon for relationship evaluation. Its state is in the tooltip.

| State | Tooltip |
|---|---|
| Running | "Evaluating relationships..." with a spinning icon |
| Done | "Relationships evaluated" and the time elapsed, a summary of the actions the evaluator applied, and a View Evaluation History button |
| Nothing evaluated | "No relationships evaluated yet" |

There is no error state. A failed evaluation clears the last-evaluation details, so the tooltip returns to "No relationships evaluated yet", and the failure is logged to the browser console only. If relationships stop updating, check the engine first.

When Kanvas applies an evaluation result and decides to skip it, it shows the notice "Skipping evaluation application", with a reason when one is known. A successful evaluation shows no message.

## Diagnosing unexpected results

1. Turn on Enable Debugger in the Options dialog. It is off by default.
2. Open the debugger and go to its Evaluation Engine tab.
3. Read the status: Initialized, Not Initialized, or Not Available. Read the engine type, WASM or SERVER, and any initialization error. The tab refreshes every second.
4. If WASM is not initialized, or results look wrong, set the engine to Meshery server, reload, and compare.
5. Make any change to re-trigger evaluation.

If the server engine also gives wrong results, file an issue that includes the engine type, any initialization error, the relationships you expected, and the design or a minimal version of it.

## Large designs

Evaluation covers the whole design regardless of which relationship layers you hide. In Adaptive render mode, Kanvas can suggest cost-saving changes when a design grows: disabling TagSets when there are more than 5, collapsing parents when there are more than 10, hiding unused components when there are more than 200, and using Wireframe mode when there are more than 100 relationships. Each suggestion appears at most once per 60 seconds.

## Related pages

- [Relationships]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/relationships/index.md" >}}): the kinds that evaluation applies.
- [Create Relationships]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designing/creating-relationships/index.md" >}}): what you create by hand.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Run a Performance Test"
url: /kanvas/guides/operating/performance-testing/index.md
description: Generate load against a Service or Ingress from the Operator canvas using a performance profile, and read the results.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Operator mode shows a live picture of your clusters. A performance test adds the missing signal: how a service responds under load. You select a Service or Ingress on the canvas, Kanvas seeds a test from it, and Meshery runs the load and keeps the result as a reusable performance profile.

## Before you start

- **Operator mode on a Meshery you run.** The hosted kanvas.new site does not offer Operator mode.
- **A target Meshery Server can reach.** Meshery Server generates the load, not your browser and not the cluster. The address you test must be routable from wherever Meshery Server runs. A `ClusterIP` address is reachable from inside the cluster only.
- **Performance permissions.** The form needs **View performance profiles** to appear, and the Run Test button needs **Run test**. See [Permissions by Role]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/permissions.md" >}}).

## Start a test

The action is named **Initiate Performance Test** and is offered on **Service** and **Ingress** resources only, the kinds that expose an endpoint. It is not offered on pods, deployments, or any other kind. Right-click the resource, or select it and use the action in the header of the Details panel.

The Performance panel opens on the canvas at 400 px wide, floating and minimizable. Only one performance panel exists: starting a test from a second resource replaces the target of the open panel. The panel hosts the Meshery performance test form, so the fields, profiles, and results are the same ones Meshery provides. Opening the panel generates no load. Nothing runs until you press **Run Test**.

## What Kanvas pre-fills

| Setting | Seeded value |
|---|---|
| Profile name | `<Kind> - <component name>`, for example `Service - checkout` |
| URL to test | The first endpoint derived from the resource, or empty |
| Concurrent requests | 10 |
| Queries per second | 20 |
| Duration | 30s |
| Load generator | `fortio` |

Change any value before you run. The form also accepts request headers, cookies, content type, request body, additional load generator options as JSON, and a certificate for TLS endpoints.

### How the URL is derived

For a Service, Kanvas builds an endpoint from the service's type and ports and seeds the first one. A service with several ports yields several endpoints; edit the URL to test another port.

| Service type | Seeded URL |
|---|---|
| `ClusterIP` (also when no type is set) | `http://<clusterIP>:<port>` |
| `LoadBalancer` | `http://<ingress IP or hostname>:<port>`. Empty until the cloud assigns an address. |
| `ExternalName` | `http://<externalName>:<port>` |
| `NodePort` | Empty. Kanvas does not know node addresses. Enter `http://<node address>:<nodePort>`. |
| Headless (`clusterIP: None`) | Seeds `http://None:<port>`. Replace it with a real address. |

For an Ingress, the URL is always empty. Enter the host and path you want to test. The seeded scheme is always `http`; change it to `https` for TLS endpoints.

## Run it and read the result

1. Edit the seeded values.
2. Press **Run Test**. Meshery first saves the settings as a performance profile (the toast reads `Performance profile <name> has been created`), then submits the load test (`Load test has been submitted`).
3. A countdown runs for the test duration. The results then render in the same panel, with a way back to the form.

The same profile can be selected and re-run later, which is what makes a test repeatable before and after a change. Results are stored in Meshery's performance results history, not in Kanvas. Profiles, schedules, comparisons between runs, and how results are interpreted are covered in [Performance Management](https://docs.meshery.io/guides/performance-management) in the Meshery documentation.

## Validation and failure modes

| Message | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Please enter a valid URL along with protocol` | The URL needs a scheme such as `http://`. |
| `Please enter a valid JSON string` | The additional options field is not valid JSON. |
| Duration rejected | Duration must be positive and end in `h`, `m`, or `s`. |
| `Failed to create performance profile` | The profile could not be saved, so the test did not start. |
| `Load test did not run with msg: <message>` | The load generator reported a failure. The message names the cause, often an unreachable endpoint. |
| `Connection to the server got disconnected. Load test might be running in the background. Please check the results page in a few.` | The result stream dropped. The test may still finish; check the results page in Meshery. |
| Permission denied block or disabled Run Test | Your role lacks **View performance profiles** or **Run test**. |
| Empty panel | The host Meshery did not supply the performance form. Use a Meshery release that includes it. |

Kanvas does not pre-check that the endpoint is reachable.

## Related

- [Resource Details]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/resource-details/index.md" >}}) shows the live state of the resource you are testing.
- [Performance Limits and Tuning]({{< ref "kanvas/advanced/performance/index.md" >}}) covers the limits of Kanvas itself on large designs.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Whiteboard on the Canvas"
url: /kanvas/guides/designing/whiteboarding/index.md
description: Sketch freehand, draw annotation lines, and add shapes, text, sections, images, and comments alongside real components.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

{{< youtube id=o58hO4RDCR4 class="yt-embed-container" >}}

*[Whiteboarding in Kanvas]({{< ref "videos/features/kanvas/whiteboarding-in-kanvas.md" >}}) (3:41) follows one late-night incident from page to postmortem on a single live design. Its page has chapters and a transcript.*

Whiteboarding lets you diagram freely on the same canvas as your infrastructure. You draw shapes, text, freehand strokes, and lines to explain intent, and they sit beside real components in one design. It is on by default and available on every plan.

Drawn objects are saved with the design and shared live with collaborators. They are components marked as annotations, so they count toward your plan's components-per-design limit. See [Designs and Components]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/designs/index.md" >}}).

This guide covers the drawing tools. For per-object operations such as copying, locking, and resizing, see [Working with Canvas Objects]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/canvas-objects/index.md" >}}).

## The dock {#step-3-utilizing-whiteboard-tools}

The dock sits at the bottom of the canvas in Designer mode. Its tools, left to right:

| Tool | Shortcut | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Select | <kbd>V</kbd> | Select, move, and configure objects. |
| Hand | <kbd>H</kbd>, or hold <kbd>Space</kbd> | Pan the canvas. |
| Components | - | Open the component palette. |
| Kubernetes | - | Open every Kubernetes component. |
| Shapes | - | Browse shape categories. |
| Comment | <kbd>M</kbd> | Drop a comment thread. |
| Image | <kbd>I</kbd> | Pick an image file and place it. |
| TextBox | <kbd>T</kbd> | Add a text box. |
| Section | <kbd>S</kbd> | Add a labeled, dashed region that holds other objects. |
| Pen | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>E</kbd> | Draw annotation lines. |
| Pencil | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>P</kbd> | Draw freehand. |
| Help Center | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>/</kbd> | Open help. |

The Pen and Pencil icons turn green while their mode is active. Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to leave a mode. Pinned models appear after a divider at the right end. See [Pin Models to the Dock]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designing/pin-model-to-dock/index.md" >}}).

![The Kanvas Designer dock](images/whiteboard-dock.png)

The dock scrolls horizontally when it overflows, and it is greyed out while the app is in an error state, for example after a failed save. In Operator mode only the Select and Hand tools, Help Center, and minimized panels remain.

### Turn tools on or off

The canvas right-click menu opens an Options dialog with these toggles, all on by default:

- **Enable Dock** hides or shows the entire dock, including component pickers, not only the drawing tools.
- **Enable Pencil** and **Enable Pen** hide or show those two icons.

Each change saves to your user preferences, so it applies to all your designs and devices. The toggles hide icons only. The keyboard shortcuts for Pen, Pencil, <kbd>M</kbd>, <kbd>T</kbd>, <kbd>S</kbd>, and <kbd>I</kbd> keep working.

![The Options dialog with Enable Dock, Enable Pencil, and Enable Pen turned on](images/canvas-options.png)

No permission key gates drawing. Tier listings show Pencil, Pen, and 500 built-in shapes on Free, Team Designer, Team Operator, and Enterprise.

## Draw freehand with the Pencil

Each stroke becomes one filled shape. Defaults are caribbean green, thickness 1, and opacity 1. There is no color or thickness control before you draw. Afterward, select the stroke and use its style toolbar to change fill color, opacity, and border.

## Draw lines with the Pen

The Pen is Connector mode. Click empty canvas to place a small terminal point, then click elsewhere to place another and join them with a line. Repeated clicks draw a connected polyline. Starting from a component's edge handle also works. Cancelling mid-draw removes the dangling point.

Pen lines are annotation edges. They explain flow and do not change any component's configuration. Style them like any edge: color, line style, arrow and curve style, label, and animation.

Pan and box selection are off while you draw with the Pen or Pencil.

## Add shapes, text, sections, images, and comments

- **Shapes.** Choose from the shape categories. A shape carries no configuration and is never deployed. You can swap any object's outline for one of 24 shapes while keeping its content, position, and size.
- **Text boxes.** Double-click to edit text inline. Text options include color, weight (regular, medium, semi bold, bold, black), underline or strikethrough, alignment, and font size.
- **Sections.** A section groups the objects dropped inside it, and they move with it.
- **Images.** Images up to 512,000 bytes are embedded in the design. Larger files are rejected.
- **Comments.** A comment opens a discussion thread on the canvas. Resolved threads disappear from the canvas until reopened. See [Review a Design with Comments]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/collaborating/reviewing-designs/index.md" >}}).

![Shapes customization on the canvas](images/shapes_introduction.gif)

## Style objects and lines

Select an object to open its toolbar. Controls appear only when the object supports them.

![The style tooltip for a text box](images/text-customization.png)

| Control | Options |
|---|---|
| Fill | 13 swatches including transparent, with opacity from 0 to 1 |
| Border | Color, style (solid, dotted, dashed, double), thickness from 0 to 25 |
| Layer order | Move to front, forward, backward, to back |
| Animation | None, blink, ripple, bounce, pulse |
| Line style | Solid, dashed, or dotted; ten curve styles; eleven arrow heads |
| Line animation | Marching ants, which shows the direction of flow |

![Editing a line's style](images/line-editing.gif)

![The marching ants animation on a line](images/marching-ants.gif)

## Collaborate

Every change, including drawn objects, syncs live between everyone in the design through a shared document over a peer-to-peer session. Each collaborator appears as an avatar in the toolbar, and live cursors and selections are shared. Undo and redo cover the shared document: components, configuration, styles, relationships, drawn objects, and layer toggles.

## Limits and behavior

- Drawn objects are saved with the design. Kanvas never deploys annotations.
- Images and text files over about 500 KB are rejected, whatever your plan.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Designer"
url: /kanvas/concepts/designer/index.md
description: How Designer mode turns a shared design document into an editable canvas, what it gates by mode and by permission, and how changes save and sync.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Designer mode is where you author a Kanvas design. You compose infrastructure from versioned components, configure each one against its schema, connect components with relationships, annotate the result, and validate or deploy it, all on one canvas that every collaborator edits at the same time. Designer works on intent: what you want to run. [Operator]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/operator/index.md" >}}) works on live state: what is running.

<figure>
  <img src="images/designer-dock.png" alt="Kanvas Designer workspace with the bottom dock of authoring tools, the Layers panel open, and the Share control in the header" />
  <figcaption>Designer: the bottom dock holds the tools for adding components and annotations, and the Layers panel controls what the canvas draws.</figcaption>
</figure>

## A design is a shared document

Everything on the canvas is an entry in one design document: every component you configure, every relationship, and every annotation you draw. The canvas draws that document. Moving a node, applying a layout, or hiding a layer writes into the design. As a result:

- Collaborators see the same canvas, including positions, locks, and layer visibility.
- Undo and redo cover every change to the document: components, configuration, styles, relationships, annotations, and layer toggles.
- Hiding a component in the Layers panel changes only what is drawn. The component stays in the design and deploys with it.

For what a design contains and how it is versioned, see [Designs]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/designs/index.md" >}}).

## Designer and Operator

| | Designer | Operator |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | Author and change a design | Inspect and act on resources running in connected clusters |
| What the canvas draws | Components, relationships, and annotations from the design document | Kubernetes resources discovered in the selected clusters |
| What you can edit | The whole design: add, configure, relate, annotate, style, lay out, delete | Nothing; live nodes are read-only |
| Actions | Validate, deploy, undeploy, share, reset design | Open a terminal, follow logs, run a performance test, open the source design |

Selection, panning, zoom, the Layers panel, and undo and redo work in both modes. Keyboard shortcuts that add or change content, such as copy, paste, duplicate, delete, Pen, and Pencil, act only in Designer.

## What you do in Designer

- **Compose from versioned components.** The palette lists models from the Meshery registry by category, and each model offers a version selector with the newest version first. Add a component by dragging or clicking, nest it by dropping it onto a compatible parent, or drop YAML, JSON, or archive files to import infrastructure as code.
- **Configure.** A new component opens its configurator, a form rendered from the component's JSON schema with the schema's defaults. Edits write to the design after a short pause and trigger validation and relationship evaluation. Switching a component to another version keeps its configuration values; validation flags any that no longer fit.
- **Relate.** Drawing an edge or nesting one component in another creates a relationship when a registry definition matches the pair. A relationship can write values from one component's configuration into another's. Kanvas re-evaluates relationships about one second after changes stop, and evaluation never blocks editing. See [Relationships]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/relationships/index.md" >}}) and [Relationship Evaluation]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/relationship-evaluation/index.md" >}}).
- **Annotate.** Shapes, text boxes, sections, images, comments, Pen connectors, and Pencil strokes explain the design without configuring infrastructure.
- **Lay out.** Six layouts rearrange the canvas: Grid, Constrained (the default), hierarchical, star, bus, and ring. A design with no saved positions is laid out automatically when it opens; otherwise Kanvas keeps the saved positions. A layout changes positions only, never configuration.
- **Validate, dry-run, deploy, and undeploy.** Kanvas checks each changed component against its schema. A badge on the component counts its validation warnings and dry-run errors. Meshery Server carries out deployment.
- **Share.** A share gives others access to the design, and anyone with a share can edit it.

## What mode gates and what permission gates

Authoring is gated by mode, not by role. Adding, configuring, duplicating, deleting, and renaming work in Designer and are blocked in Operator. Resources synced from a live cluster are read-only in every mode. Within Designer, what you can change on a component depends on that component's registry capabilities: a configurator tab or a style control appears only when the component declares it.

Only four actions are permission-gated: validate, deploy, undeploy, and share. When your role lacks one of these permissions, its control is hidden. The permission catalog also lists permissions for individual canvas gestures, such as adding shapes or resetting styles. Kanvas does not enforce those on the canvas, so withholding them has no effect. Users who are not signed in are prompted to sign in before sharing, and to sign in or run Meshery locally before validating or deploying. See [Permissions]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/permissions.md" >}}).

## How changes are stored and synchronized

Designer has no Save button. Every change to the design requests a save, and Kanvas sends it 3 seconds after the last change. A new design is not saved until it has a component or a name.

While a design is open, every change, drawn objects included, syncs live between collaborators through the shared document. Each collaborator appears as an avatar in the toolbar, and their cursor and current selection show on your canvas. Storage does not merge: each save sends the whole design, and the last save wins. Live co-editing in the open session is what reconciles concurrent edits. See [Collaboration]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/collaboration/index.md" >}}).

If a save fails, Kanvas enters an error state: the dock is disabled and edits are not applied while Kanvas retries the save with increasing delays.

## Configurable components and annotations

Every object on the canvas is a component entry in the design. Annotations carry an annotation flag; configurable components do not. The Layers panel uses that flag to split the canvas into Annotations and Configurable Components, each with a count and its own visibility toggle. Pen connectors are non-binding annotation relationships: they draw lines without changing any configuration.

The distinction does not exempt annotations from your plan. When a design is saved, Layer5 Cloud counts every component entry, annotations included, against the components-per-design limit. The limit is checked on save, not when you add an object, so a design can grow past it on the canvas and then fail to save.

## What Designer does not do

- It does not operate live workloads. Terminal sessions, log streams, and performance tests are Operator actions.
- It does not filter components by label. Label filters exist only in Operator views.
- It does not set an access level on a share. Every share can edit.
- It does not narrow relationship evaluation by layer. Evaluation always covers the whole design.

## Where to go next

- Reference: [Canvas Objects]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/canvas-objects/index.md" >}}), [Tool Modes]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/tool-modes/index.md" >}}), [Canvas Actions]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/canvas-actions/index.md" >}}), [Layout and Layers]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/layout-and-layers/index.md" >}}), [Component Badges]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/component-badges/index.md" >}}), and [Keyboard Shortcuts]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/keyboard-shortcuts.md" >}}).
- Build a design: [Configuring Components]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designing/configuring-components/index.md" >}}), [Creating Relationships]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designing/creating-relationships/index.md" >}}), and [Whiteboarding]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designing/whiteboarding/index.md" >}}).
- Check and save a design: [Validating Designs]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/deploying/validating-designs/index.md" >}}) and [Saving Designs]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designs/saving-designs/index.md" >}}).
- Give others access: [Sharing Designs]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/collaborating/sharing-designs/index.md" >}}).


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Export Designs"
url: /kanvas/guides/designs/export-designs/index.md
description: Export a design as a design file, an OCI image, a Kubernetes manifest, a Helm chart, or an embeddable script, and know what each format keeps.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Export writes a design out of Kanvas so you can back it up, move it between Meshery deployments, hand it to Helm or `kubectl`, or put it on a web page. Every export is generated from the current state of the design. You cannot export an earlier version.

Export is a File menu action, disabled on an empty design. In Operator mode, Export instead downloads the open view as `<view name>.json`.

## Choose a format

| Format | Keeps layout, annotations, and metadata | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| Design file (YAML) | Yes | Backups, moving designs, re-import into Kanvas |
| Design (OCI image) | Yes | Storing and versioning a design in a container registry |
| Kubernetes manifest | No | `kubectl apply` and pipelines that expect plain manifests |
| Helm chart | No | Helm repositories, Argo CD, Flux, Artifact Hub |
| Embed design (JavaScript) | Snapshot of the canvas | Showing a design on a web page |

Kanvas offers at least one of the first four. Which ones appear can depend on the capabilities of your Layer5 Cloud account. Per-format options and size limits are not exposed. To capture the canvas as a PNG picture, use Take Screenshot instead. See [Canvas Actions]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/canvas-actions/index.md" >}}).

## Design file (YAML) {#exporting-as-a-design-file}

A complete copy of the design, including layout, annotations, component grouping, and configuration. The download is named `<design name>.yml`. Kanvas can import it back without loss.

## Design (OCI image) {#exporting-as-an-oci-image}

The same lossless content packaged as an OCI image archive. Push it with a registry tool such as `docker push` or `oras push` to version and distribute designs alongside application artifacts. Kanvas imports the archive back, taking the design file in its layers. See [Import and Merge Designs]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designs/import-designs/index.md" >}}).

## Source-type formats {#exporting-in-a-source-type-format}

A design can be exported as the kind of source it was built from. Both formats are lossy: layout, annotations, and comments are dropped because neither format can carry them. To keep a design fully editable, export the design file instead.

Docker Compose is an import source only. A design cannot be exported to Compose.

### Kubernetes manifest {#exporting-as-a-kubernetes-manifest}

Plain Kubernetes resource definitions, ready for `kubectl apply`.

### Helm chart {#exporting-as-a-helm-chart}

A `.tar.gz` chart archive that contains the Kubernetes resource definitions. Install it with `helm install <release> <chart>.tgz` or place it in a Helm repository.

Re-importing a manifest or chart restores the resources, but not the layout, so the graph does not reappear as you drew it.

## Embed design (JavaScript) {#exporting-as-embedding}

The Embed Design option downloads a JavaScript module and shows a two-line snippet to paste into an HTML page. The embed is a static snapshot, not a live view. See [Embed Designs]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designs/embedding-designs/index.md" >}}).

## Access and tiers

- Exporting needs no sign-in for a public or published design. Anonymous callers can download the design file of any public or published design, not just their own. A private design is downloadable by its owner, a provider administrator, a user the design is shared with, or a user holding the View Designs permission.
- Each download of the design file writes an audit event and raises the design's download count. Anonymous downloads record as "Anonymous viewer downloaded".
- No plan tier gates export, and exporting your own design needs no permission key. Layer5 Cloud's catalog table shows its Download action to roles with the Download a Design permission.
- The browser either prompts for a save location or saves to your downloads folder. Success shows `<name> design downloaded`. Failure shows "Failed to download design".

## Keep a version you can return to

A design has a single current version, and the save history is an event log, not a set of snapshots. To keep a restorable point, export a design file or an OCI image at that moment and store it. For an OCI image, push it to a registry under a tag.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Pin Models to the Dock"
url: /kanvas/guides/designing/pin-model-to-dock/index.md
description: Keep the models you use most one step away in the dock, and remove them when you no longer need them.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Pinning a model puts its icon in the dock at the bottom of the canvas, so you can reach its components without opening the full palette. Pins belong to your account. They are not stored per design or in the browser, so they follow you across designs, browsers, and devices.

Pinning works in Designer mode. In Operator mode the dock does not show pinned models.

## Pin a model

Hover a model row in the component palette and use the pin icon. Its tooltip reads "Pin To Dock". The shape palette offers the same pin on each shape category row.

![The Pin To Dock action on a model in the component list](images/pin-to-dock.png)

Only models and shape categories can be pinned. Individual components cannot. There is no limit on how many models you pin. Kanvas matches pins by model name, so pinning the same model at a different version is the same pin.

## Use a pinned model

Pinned models appear after a divider at the right end of the dock.

![A pinned model displayed in the dock](images/pinned-model-location.png)

Select a pinned model to open a picker with its components. Click a component to add it near the center of the canvas, or drag it to a specific spot. The picker has its own search box and a version selector with an "All Versions" choice. A pinned model whose lookup returns nothing is not drawn.

![Components of a pinned model in the picker](images/use-pinned-models-components.png)

## Remove a pin

Either of these removes the pin without affecting any design:

- Select the pin icon again on the model row. Its tooltip reads "Remove From Dock".
- Hover the pinned model in the dock and select the close (X) badge.

![The Remove From Dock action](images/unpin-model-1.png)

![Unpinning with the close badge](images/unpin-model-2.png)

## Default dock

With nothing pinned the dock holds Select, Hand, Components, Kubernetes, Shapes, Comment, Image, TextBox, Section, Pen, Pencil, and Help Center. See [Whiteboard on the Canvas]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designing/whiteboarding/index.md" >}}).


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Tool Modes"
url: /kanvas/reference/tool-modes/index.md
description: Reference for the Designer tool modes - Select, Pan, Pencil and Pen - covering how to enter and leave each, what the mouse does in each, and how wheel and zoom controls behave.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The canvas has four tool modes. The mode decides what a mouse drag does: move an object, pan the view, draw freehand or draw a connecting line. Select is the default. This page lists how to enter and leave each mode, what every mouse gesture does in it, and the wheel and zoom controls that work in all of them.

## Modes at a glance

| Mode | Purpose | Enter | Leave | Drag on empty canvas | Box selection |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Select | Select, move, configure and style objects. The default. | <kbd>V</kbd> or <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Choose another mode | Draws a selection box | On |
| Pan | Move the view without touching objects. | <kbd>H</kbd>, or hold <kbd>Space</kbd> | <kbd>V</kbd>, <kbd>Esc</kbd>, or release <kbd>Space</kbd> | Pans the view | Off |
| Pencil | Draw freehand annotations. | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>P</kbd>, or the Pencil tool in the dock | The same shortcut, <kbd>V</kbd> or <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Draws a stroke | Off |
| Pen | Draw connecting lines and annotation edges. | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>E</kbd>, or the Pen tool in the dock | The same shortcut, <kbd>V</kbd> or <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Places points and lines | Off |

The Pencil and Pen dock icons turn green while their mode is active. The mode shortcuts work in Designer mode. Select and Pan also work in Operator mode.

Releasing <kbd>Space</kbd> returns you to Select, not to the mode you held it from. If you were drawing with Pencil or Pen, re-enter that mode afterward.

Kanvas ignores single-key shortcuts while you type in a text field, so typing a label or a comment never changes the mode.

## Select mode

| Gesture | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Hover | No effect. |
| Click an object | Selects it and shows its style toolbar, resize handles and connection handles. |
| Drag an object | Moves it. Locked objects do not move. |
| Double-click a component | Opens its configurator. |
| Double-click a textbox or comment | Edits its text inline. |
| Right-click, or press and hold, on an object | Opens the object menu. |
| Right-click on empty canvas | Opens the canvas menu. See [Canvas Actions]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/canvas-actions/index.md" >}}). |
| Drag on empty canvas | Draws a selection box that selects the objects it covers. |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + click | Adds an object to the selection or removes it. |

The cursor shows an arrow while hovering, a move cursor while dragging an object and a crosshair while you draw a selection box.

![Selecting several objects with a selection box in Select mode](images/select.gif)

Object actions are listed in [Canvas Objects]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/canvas-objects/index.md" >}}).

## Pan mode

Pan mode turns a drag on the canvas into a pan. The cursor is an open hand, and a closed hand while you drag. Hold <kbd>Space</kbd> to pan for as long as the key is down, or press <kbd>H</kbd> to stay in Pan mode until you leave it.

## Pencil mode

Pencil draws freehand. Each stroke you release becomes one annotation object on the canvas.

| Gesture | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Press and drag | Draws a freehand stroke. |
| Release | Completes the stroke and turns it into an object. |

A new stroke is caribbean green, with thickness 1 and full opacity. Pencil has no color or thickness control before you draw. Select the stroke afterward and change its fill, border and opacity in the style toolbar. See [Canvas Objects]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/canvas-objects/index.md" >}}).

Pencil strokes connect to nothing. They annotate. Pan and box selection are off while Pencil is active.

![Drawing a freehand stroke in Pencil mode](images/pencil.gif)

## Pen mode

Pen draws lines. Each line is an annotation edge, a non-binding relationship that carries no configuration, so it explains a design without changing it.

| Step | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Click on empty canvas | Places a small point to start from. |
| Click again elsewhere on empty canvas | Places another point and draws an edge between the two. Repeating this draws a connected line of segments. |
| Start from a component's connection handle and release on another component or a point | Draws an edge between them. |
| Cancel mid-draw | Removes the dangling point. |

Points are small borderless shapes. Edges drawn with Pen use the same style controls as every other edge: color, line style, curve, arrowhead, label and animation. See [Canvas Objects]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/canvas-objects/index.md" >}}). Pan and box selection are off while Pen is active.

Edges between registry-defined components, which configure the components they join, are drawn in Select mode from a component's connection handle. See [Relationships]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/relationships/index.md" >}}).

## Wheel and zoom controls

These are registered in Designer and Operator mode.

| Input | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Scroll wheel | Pans vertically. |
| Horizontal scroll, or <kbd>Shift</kbd> + scroll wheel | Pans horizontally. Each <kbd>Shift</kbd> step moves 50 pixels. |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + scroll wheel | Zooms toward the pointer. Each step changes the zoom by 0.1. |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>+</kbd> and <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>-</kbd> | Zooms in and out by the same step. |

The Options drawer sets the zoom range: a minimum from 0.1 to 5 (default 0.1) and a maximum from 0.1 to 30 (default 30). Zooming the page itself is left to the browser.

Object controls and badges appear only when the canvas is zoomed in far enough. When you are zoomed out, Kanvas shows a hint to zoom in to interact with elements.

## Related reading

- [Keyboard Shortcuts]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/keyboard-shortcuts.md" >}}) - every shortcut in one list.
- [Whiteboarding]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/designing/whiteboarding/index.md" >}}) - a task guide to drawing on a design.
- [Designer]({{< ref "kanvas/concepts/designer/index.md" >}}) - what Designer mode is for.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Undeploy a Design"
url: /kanvas/guides/deploying/undeploying-designs/index.md
description: Remove the resources a design describes from your clusters, and understand exactly what is and is not deleted.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Undeploying deletes the Kubernetes objects that each component in a design describes, from every cluster in the environments you select. It does not touch the design itself. The design record, its versions, and its Operator view are unchanged.

## Before you start

The prerequisites match [Deploy a Design]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/deploying/deploying-designs/index.md" >}}): a Meshery you run with a connected cluster, a non-empty design, and the **Undeploy Design** permission. The hosted kanvas.new site does not run undeploy. See [Permissions by Role]({{< ref "kanvas/reference/permissions.md" >}}).

## The undeploy flow

Choose Undeploy from the design's Actions menu. The `Undeploy design "<name>"` stepper has the same five steps and gates as the deploy stepper:

1. **Validate Design.** Runs validation inline.
2. **Identify Environments.** Selects the environments, and so the clusters, to remove from.
3. **Dry Run.** An undeploy-type [dry run]({{< ref "kanvas/guides/deploying/dry-running-a-design/index.md" >}}) that deletes by name with server-side dry run. Because an absent object returns NotFound, a design that was never deployed, or is already removed, shows an error for every component here and needs the bypass checkbox to continue.
4. **Finalize.** Confirms the environments and component count. The button reads Undeploy.
5. **Finish.** Runs the removal and shows the results.

## What gets deleted

| Behavior | Detail |
|---|---|
| What is removed | One delete for each non-annotation component's object, in its namespace, on every selected cluster. |
| How it is matched | By kind and name from the design, not by label. An object with the same kind and name that was created some other way is deleted too. |
| Order | Reverse dependency order. A component whose dependent failed to delete is withheld: `Withheld <component>: <dependent> did not undeploy successfully`. |
| Objects already gone | Ignored. |
| Namespaces, custom resource definitions, volume claims, Secrets | Deleted only when the design has a component for them. |
